claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: For a fixed supply φ and an absorbing boundary T, set d_z(v)=z(v,s_0(v))−z(v,s_1(v)). Summing (y−x)(u,v)(h_t(u)−h_t(v)) by vertices cancels every nonterminal through equal conservation laws and leaves x^−(t)−y^−(t). Summing by outgoing pairs instead gives Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v). Since d_x,d_y∈[0,1] and harmonicity gives |g_t(v)|=|h_t(s_1(v))−h_t(s_0(v))|/2≤1/2, every terminal coordinate has diameter at most N/2. Total boundary inflow is Σ_vφ(v), so the last coordinate is determined and there are at most (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(|T|−1) integral signatures. For φ≡1, prescribed imbalances are realizable: the transient nonterminal transition matrix makes the displayed affine system uniquely solvable, iteration from t=1 remains at least 1, and (t_v±d_v)/2 are nonnegative switching-flow values. Thus choosing endpoint imbalances according to sign(g_t) also proves sharpness of the harmonic diameter formula.
claims.witness: For φ(v)=1, choose d_y(v)=1,d_x(v)=0 when g_t(v)>0 and d_y(v)=0,d_x(v)=1 when g_t(v)<0; the resulting flows differ at terminal t by exactly Σ_v|g_t(v)|.
claims.search_method: Derived both evaluations of the harmonic edge sum from the authorized switching-flow definition, checked transience and nonnegativity of the realization construction, and tested the identities with exact rational arithmetic on the parametric families.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: An edge from level j cannot go below level j−1. Because the finite uniform walk is absorbing, a walk starting at any level at least i hits L_{i−1} almost surely before a sink. Optional stopping at that first hit expresses its hitting probability as a convex combination of values on L_{i−1}. Hence [m_i,M_i]⊆[m_{i−1},M_{i−1}]. Both successors of v∈L_i consequently have values in that preceding interval, so |g(v)|≤W_{i−1}/2. Summing over r vertices on every positive level yields Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_iW_{i−1}≤rk/2. The family in claim 2 has Θ(k) actual gap mass, so linear growth is genuinely possible rather than merely an artifact of the estimate.
claims.witness: The width-three k-level family of claim 2 has W_i=1−i/(k+1) and gap mass k(k+7)/(4(k+1))=Θ(k).
claims.search_method: Proved the first-hit convex-combination statement from the distance-level definition and checked nesting, the vertexwise inequality, and its sum exactly for k=2,…,14 and widths 3,…,7.

claims.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
claims.evidence: Substitution in the stated k-level graph gives h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1−i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. The a- and b-gaps contribute k/(k+1), while the c-gaps contribute k(k+3)/[4(k+1)], totaling D=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). Claim 0's φ≡1 realization chooses imbalance endpoints attaining terminal-inflow separation D, proving unbounded same-supply diameter. For k=2, exact conservation checks confirm both listed flows have supply 1 at every nonsink, all even-minus-odd imbalances lie in [0,1], and their sink-1 inflows are 10/3 and 11/6, separated by 3/2>1. Adding r−3 half-valued vertices per level preserves levels and harmonic values and changes the mass to k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)], as claimed.
claims.search_method: Recomputed all harmonic equations and gap sums symbolically, checked directed distances, and verified the concrete and parametric flows using fractions only.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
claims.evidence: The two completions have identical sinks and identical outgoing edges from a,b,c in L1, and exact reverse-distance computation places a,b,c in L1 and X,Y,Z in L2. In completion A, harmonicity gives c=1/2, a=X/2, b=Y/2, X=(c+b)/2, and Y=(a+b)/2, whose unique solution has (a,b)=(3/22,1/22). In completion B, X=(a+b)/2 and Y=(c+a)/2 instead, producing (a,b)=(1/22,3/22). Thus identical preceding-level order and identical local L1 outgoing data yield opposite orders of a and b.
claims.witness: Completion A: X→(c,b), Y→(a,b), giving h(a)>h(b). Completion B: X→(a,b), Y→(c,a), giving h(a)<h(b). Common edges are a→(0,X), b→(0,Y), c→(0,1), Z→(a,c).
claims.search_method: Solved both finite harmonic systems by exact Gauss-Jordan elimination and independently checked their level decompositions and equality of local data.

claims.claim: For fixed supply and a fixed number of terminals, all feasible integral boundary signatures of real switching flows can be enumerated in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: The real switching flows form a rational polyhedron. Terminal inflows are nonnegative and sum to S=Σ_vφ(v), so every coordinate objective is bounded and its rational LP extrema α_t,β_t are attained. Claim 0 gives β_t−α_t≤N/2. For any fixed set of r terminals, each of the first r−1 coordinates therefore has at most ⌊N/2⌋+1 candidate integers. Their Cartesian product has polynomial size for fixed r; the last coordinate is S minus their sum. An exact rational LP with those terminal equalities accepts precisely the realizable tuples. LP input sizes remain polynomial because the extrema and candidate integers have polynomial bit length. The argument concerns integral terminal signatures of real edge flows and does not assume edge integrality.
claims.search_method: Audited boundedness, attainment, rational bit complexity, candidate completeness, the forced final coordinate, and exact LP feasibility; also constructed and checked the enumerated integer signatures on the width-three family.

claims.claim: At positive-level width three, one fixed integer supply can admit Θ(N) distinct integral sink-inflow signatures among real switching flows.
claims.evidence: For the width-three family, N=3k and the two φ≡1 flows have sink-1 inflows separated by D=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). The feasible switching-flow set is convex because conservation, nonnegativity, and 0≤x_0−x_1≤1 are linear constraints. Convex combinations therefore realize every sink-1 value in the closed interval between the two endpoints. That interval contains at least ⌊D⌋=Θ(k)=Θ(N) integers, and total terminal inflow is N, so each yields a distinct integral signature (q,N−q). Claim 0 bounds all two-terminal integral signatures by ⌊N/2⌋+1, supplying the matching O(N) bound.
claims.witness: For each integer q between the two endpoint inflows, λ=(q−A)/(B−A) and the convex flow (1−λ)x+λy has signature (q,3k−q). Exact constructions were checked for k=2,…,14.
claims.search_method: Combined the exact endpoint construction with a convexity proof, then generated every intervening integral signature using rational λ and rechecked all switching-flow constraints exactly.

target_evidence: The exact wording includes L0, which always consists of the two sinks, so a literal r>2 class would be empty. The draft correctly identifies that mismatch and addresses the intended nonvacuous interpretation—r vertices in every positive level. Under that requested interpretation, the draft does not determine polynomial-time solvability for r=3 or for every fixed r>2. Its verified fixed-supply signature compression and its counterexamples to two width-two mechanisms are material structural progress, but they neither bound the varying suffix supplies arising in the recursion nor give an ARRIVAL algorithm, hardness result, or complete classification. The final writeup explicitly acknowledges this limitation, so target coverage is valid but incomplete and claimed_resolution="PARTIAL" is accurate.
